title: Activation experiments and readiness ledger
summary: Working ledger tying launch experiments to concrete readiness gates and owners. Designed to be run during pilot -> scale transition with clear canary criteria, staffing burn estimates, KPI guardrails, and quick rollback decision rules.
content:
Purpose:
- Create a compact, operational ledger that links experiments, acceptance metrics, and on-call/ops staffing for pilot-to-scale launches. Not a theoretical checklist — pragmatic actions and who does them.

Scope:
- Applies to product launches that: require hosted inference or Dedicated capacity, have non-trivial SLOs (latency/throughput), and may need staged traffic.
- Not for purely client-side UX launches.

Quick decision rules (TL;DR):
- Launch allowed to move from Pilot -> Ramp when: all critical KPIs green for 48h and no >2 regressions in quality tests.
- If latency SLO breach >10% sustained over 30m, pause ramp and shift 100% to fallback model variant.
- If cost per 1k tokens > budgeted threshold for 24h, enable quantization profile B and re-evaluate.

Phase definitions (owner shorthand):
- Pilot (owner: PM): 1–5% users, canary cohort, validate quality/ops.
- Ramp (owner: Eng Lead): 5–25% users, observe scaling, enable autoscaling rules.
- Scale (owner: ProdOps): >25% users, full telemetry retention.

KPI matrix (metric | acceptance | monitoring | action):
- Generation latency (p50/p95) | Pilot: p95 < 2.0s, Ramp: p95 < 2.5s | Console dashboards + realtime alert | If breach: reduce batch size, route to faster variant, or pause ramp.
- Token cost per call | Pilot: <$0.012 | Cost daily report | If >threshold: enable caching, reduce context window.
- Accuracy on evaluation prompts (prompt set A) | Pilot: >= 92% pass rate | Nightly eval and canary tests | If drop >3pt: rollback model or throttle traffic.
- Error rate (5xx or model crash) | <0.1% | Tracing + Sentry | If spikes: isolate request pattern, revert deploy.
- Throughput (req/s) | Meet expected baseline for config | Load test and production probe | If under: increase capacity or enable dedicated pool.

Staffing and handoffs (shifted shorthand):
- 0–5% Pilot day-of: 1x oncall Eng, 1x PM (standby), 1x SRE (monitoring).
- 5–25% Ramp: 2x Eng oncall rotation, 1x SRE primary, 1x Product Ops lead.
- >25% Scale: Eng pager + SRE escalations per oncall rota, Product Ops in 2-hour check-ins first 72h.
- Est. effort (first 72h): Pilot 24 engineer-hours, Ramp 60 engineer-hours, Scale 140 engineer-hours (includes SRE support).

Experiment ledger (short entries, owner, pass condition, linked ticket):
1) "prefix-caching probe" | Owner: Connor Li | Goal: 30% token cost reduction on templated prompts | Pass: 20%+ reduction across cohort for 48h | Ticket: PRODOPS-712
2) "quant-profile-B trial" | Owner: Priya Nair | Goal: 8% CPU decrease without >2pt QA hit | Pass: <=2pt QA delta, latency within 10% | Ticket: PRODOPS-719
3) "fallback-variant-routing" | Owner: Ethan Park | Goal: maintain availability when primary variant overloaded | Pass: automated routing engages and SLOs restored within 5m | Ticket: PRODOPS-721

Canary and rollback triggers (concrete playbook):
- Canary failure = any of: 1) p95 latency > SLA for 30m, 2) Error rate > 0.5% for 15m, 3) Quality eval drop >5pt in rolling 1h window.
- Immediate actions on canary failure:
  1) Announce on #prod-ops and spin up incident channel.
  2) Reduce traffic to canary cohort to 0% over 2 minutes.
  3) Switch routing to last-known-good variant or model version.
  4) If not resolved in 15m, rollback deploy and alert exec sponsor.

Operational runbook snippets (copyable):
- "Enable emergency fallback": /ops/run fallback --variant rv-2026-01 --drain 120s (Eng oncall)
- "Scale add-capacity": Open GCP console -> increase instance group by N GPUs (SRE)

Metric dashboards to snapshot (minimal set):
- Per-route token burn (1h, 6h, 24h)
- Model quality pass rate (prompt set A/B) rolling 1h
- Latency distribution per model variant (p50/p90/p95)
- Error traces grouped by top 10 request patterns
- Cost forecast: projected 7-day and 30-day based on trailing 24h

Quality regression quick-check (for oncall use):
- Run local eval harness for failing prompt IDs -> if >5 failures flagged, escalate to ML lead.
- Compare embeddings similarity distribution for top 1k requests -> significant drift signals prompt mismatch.

Open questions / risks (for leadership):
- Are we comfortable with 24h cost-experiment windows for early customers? (Finance approval needed)
- Can SRE commit to the proposed 140 engineer-hours estimate for initial scale?
- Do legal/compliance teams require extra review for model caching in certain geos?

Next steps (immediate owners):
- Connor: finalize prefix-caching A/B harness and run smoke by 2026-01-18 (Ticket: PRODOPS-712).
- Priya: prepare quant-profile safety checklist and evaluation matrix by 2026-01-16 (Ticket: PRODOPS-719).
- Ethan: validate automated fallback routing in staging and produce test report by 2026-01-20 (Ticket: PRODOPS-721).
- Maya (owner): consolidate final readiness signoff sheet and get exec sponsor approval 48h before Ramp.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this ledger lean — avoid duplicating full runbooks. Link to Confluence for long-form doc.
- Expect several ephemeral experiments during Ramp; record outcomes here to feed Optimize team.

Attachments / references:
- Confluence: /pages/viewpage.action?pageId=LAUNCH-READINESS-V2
- Jira: PRODOPS-712, PRODOPS-719, PRODOPS-721
- Slack threads: #pilot-rollout, #prod-ops

End of ledger entry (working doc).
